subject.title: fix(cron): default deleteAfterRun for isolated cron jobs

question: Should recurring isolated cron jobs be cleanup-safe by default, or should recurring `deleteAfterRun` remain an invalid one-shot-only lifecycle contract?
rationale: Two open PRs encode opposite cron lifecycle contracts, and the choice affects upgrades, session retention, and whether existing omitted persisted rows need migration or operator recovery.

options.title: Complete recurring cleanup
options.body: Keep this PR's direction, but require persisted-row repair or doctor/load coverage and preserve explicit `deleteAfterRun: false`.

options.title: Reject recurring delete-after-run
options.body: Choose the strict-validation direction and pause or close this PR after documenting recovery for affected users.

options.title: Accept fresh-create-only default
options.body: Land the default only for newly created jobs and explicitly accept that existing omitted jobs need operator action or a later migration.

recommendation.title: Complete recurring cleanup
recommendation.body: Keep this PR's direction, but require persisted-row repair or doctor/load coverage and preserve explicit `deleteAfterRun: false`.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision spans cron normalization, SQLite store upgrade behavior, and compatibility policy where steipete has recent central commits.
